answer.rationale: The 18% cost-cut mandate is unmet by the incumbent, who has refused to reopen price. memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit-cost cuts last year, with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—so the operational risk of a primary switch is already partially de-risked. memory_c4 shows that when price is non-negotiable with the incumbent, real margin recovery comes from switching, not from negotiation. The line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, which makes a hard, immediate full switch too risky. I am therefore framing this as a small, guarded pilot transfer to the low-cost vendor while retaining the incumbent under a short bridge—so I can validate the c2 onboarding/invoicing record on a live but bounded share of volume before scaling. This uses exactly one sourcing decision this cycle, meets the mandate on the transferred share, and limits delivery-risk exposure given the absence of buffer capacity. The next-cycle review can scale up or roll back based on the pilot.
